title: Buyer Sentiment Competitive Implication Study
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Summary: We will run a mixed-method research initiative to surface early buyer sentiment signals that predict competitive switching or procurement acceleration for inference platforms. The goal is to translate qualitative signals (buyer interviews, win/loss notes) and quantitative telemetry (latency tolerances, pricing sensitivity) into a compact set of competitive implications for sales and product strategy.

Scope: Focus on mid-market and enterprise product teams in EU financial and healthcare verticals for the first phase. Include self-serve SMB patterns as a secondary lens. Exclude model-level microbenchmarks (we will link to existing model-scout docs).

Hypothesis: Recent buyer hesitancy centers on three axes: predictable latency under peak load, transparent unit economics for embeddings/query-heavy workflows, and integration friction for VPC/private deployments. If we can detect shifts in buyer language and procurement behavior across these axes, we can proactively surface tactical product changes and sales playbook updates that reduce deal cycle time.

Approach: 1) Rapid buyer interviews (10 customers + 5 prospects) using a standardized script. 2) Structured analysis of sales win/loss notes (last 18 months) and support tickets labeled "latency" or "pricing". 3) Telemetry sweep: aggregate per-customer 95th percentile latency and token-cost-per-session for top 50 accounts. 4) Competitive scan: weekly scrape of competitor published latency SLAs, published pricing tiers, and any new private offering announcements. 5) Synthesis into a short implications memo and 3 prioritized tactical recommendations for product and GTM.

Deliverables: a 12-slide synthesis deck, a 2-page executive memo, a Looker dashboard prototype with buyer-sentiment flags, and a prioritized actions backlog for product and sales.

Competitive scan shows two vendors advertising tightened SLAs and one vendor introducing a VPC 'private plane' bundle targeted at regulated customers.
